entry.title: Day 4: The Girl Who Held the Door Shut
entry.content:
Plant into the burn.a Second Growth sticker on a bus shelter

At the desk Isabel asked again about the kiss.

Natalie did not answer. She took Isabel's coat from the chair and the phone from the desk and carried them into the bathroom. The door stuck on its swollen frame. She set both palms flat against it and pushed until the lock caught. The burn opened under the wrap and wept through. Afterward she could not close her fingers.

Before morning the ash under the fire stair, left from Isabel's blaze-out, sent green into every dead planter box and cracked grate in the lane. Stems came up through the drains. Buds opened in midwinter. Neighbours came down in raincoats and slippers and held their phones over it. The photos went into Isabel's chat one after another. Behind the bathroom door the phone lit blue and buzzed against the tiles.

In the north lanes the Hundred and Ninth: Creeping Knotweed grew nerves again.

Isabel went down with no coat. The lane was full of people and leaves. She crouched at the first planter and did not get up for a long time. The drizzle had turned to rain. It soaked her to the skin. When she climbed back up she was shaking harder than when she had gone down. Her hands had stiffened in the cold and would not hold the rail.

Off Linden Rise, Amara Nwosu followed a buzz down into the wet dark. She told no one. She came out in a lane she did not know, shoes full of water. Nothing had been cut.

Hyejin Park wrote to a novice girl. Three messages: what it costs, how girls die, that nobody is coming. The girl started a reply and stopped partway through a sentence. Nothing else came from that handle. Hyejin had her own three messages on the screen. The girl stayed home.

Log

  • The ash from Isabel's blaze-out under the fire stair drives every dead planter box and cracked grate in the lane into flower overnight, in midwinter; the neighbours come out in the rain with their phones, and the photos land in Isabel's chat. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 4)
    • Blight in the north lanes grows nerves again +1
    • Natalie now believes: Flowers in midwinter off a burned-out cut mean the ground in that lane has gone fat, and the blight will come for it — she will have to walk the lane herself before it does.
  • Amara follows the buzz down into the wet dark off Linden Rise alone, telling no one, and comes out in a lane she doesn't know with her shoes full of water and nothing cut.
    • Amara Nwosu now believes: Whatever is at the far end of the buzz is no bigger than the last two, and she can take it alone without anyone at home ever knowing.
  • Hyejin sends a novice girl the plain version nobody sent her — what it costs, how girls die, that nobody is coming — and the girl goes quiet and stays home. (success-with-cost, controlled, rolled 2, 4)
    • Hyejin Park lost the girl's replies — the thread goes dead mid-sentence and Hyejin is left with her own three blunt messages and no one at that handle who will ever write to her again
    • Hyejin Park now believes: The girl stayed home — one more who won't die learning alone, and the warning did what a warning can do.
  • Isabel goes down in the rain to the fire-stair lane to look at midwinter flowers the ash from her blaze-out put there, while the neighbours are still out photographing them. (success-with-cost, controlled, rolled 4, 3)
    • Isabel hurt: down in the sideways rain on no sleep: soaked to the skin and shaking harder than when she left, hands aching and stiff in the cold
  • Natalie refuses to answer Isabel about the kiss — she takes Isabel's coat and phone and locks them in the bathroom instead — and the burn across both palms splits open again forcing the door. (failure, desperate, rolled 2, 2)
    • Natalie hurt: the burn across both palms splits open again forcing the bathroom door shut, weeping through the wrap, and she can't properly close her fingers (2)
    • Isabel now believes: Natalie locked her coat and her phone in the bathroom rather than answer, so the kiss is the answer — Natalie has decided it was a mistake, and so is she.
    • Natalie now believes: Locking the phone in the bathroom bought a night, not an answer; Iz will read the door as the answer and act on it.

entry.title: Day 3: The Girl Who Would Not Stay Put
entry.content:
Linden Rise Drain Lake. No swimming. No fishing. Dogs on leads at all times.a council sign at the lake's east gate

The desk lamp was the only light in the flat, amber on the wood. Rain drove against the window from the river side. Across the water the south ridge towers kept their red pulse.

Natalie sat with her hands palm-up on a folded towel. The dressings were two days old. Isabel had changed them once and was due to again at one.

Isabel put the roll of gauze down. She asked whether Natalie had taken the cut out of her hands because of last night. She said the word kiss. Then she picked the gauze back up.

Natalie did not answer.

Isabel's phone lit blue on the desk. A post in Bay Sightings, from a handle with no history. Something big near the drain lake at Linden Rise. Is it ok to go alone.

The same minute, in the north lanes, the Hundred and Ninth: Creeping Knotweed grew nerves again, through the crooked seam where it had been closed.

Isabel read the post aloud. She read out the tram line, the stop, the walk from the stop to the east gate, fourteen minutes in this weather.

Natalie stood. She took Isabel's coat off the chair and the phone off the desk, one in each hand. The grip split the burn across both palms. Blood came through the gauze and onto the collar of the coat. She said stay here. She said it twice.

Isabel took her spare coat from the hook by the door. The route was already in her head. She was down the first flight of stairs before Natalie had the door shut behind her.

Log

  • A first-ever post from an unknown handle lands in Bay Sightings — something big near the drain lake at Linden Rise, is it ok to go alone — and Isabel's phone lights up on the desk with it, and whatever is out there near the water has now been seen. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 5)
    • Blight in the north lanes grows nerves again +1
  • Isabel asks Natalie point-blank whether she took the cut out of her hands because of last night, and the question is out of her mouth and cannot be put back. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 5)
    • Isabel lost the silence she had kept about the kiss — she has asked the question out loud and it cannot be taken back
  • Natalie lifts Isabel's coat and phone off the desk and orders her to stay put, and the grab splits the burn across her palms, and the order doesn't hold. (failure, desperate, rolled 3, 3)
    • Natalie hurt: the burn across her palms, split open again when she grabbed Iz's coat and phone off the desk
    • Isabel and Natalie -1
    • Isabel now believes: Natalie took the cut out of her hands and then took her coat and her phone off the desk because of last night — the kiss is why she can't be trusted with the work.
    • Isabel now believes: Natalie has already decided about the kiss and isn't going to say it; the coat and the phone off the desk are the answer.
    • Natalie now believes: Ordering Iz to stay put has never held anyone, and it has just cost her the use of her hands again.

entry.title: Day 2: The Girl Who Was Called Away Across the Water
entry.content:
Old core residents: do not cross flooded canals on foot. Move to higher floors. Do not reply to this message.a municipal flood alert, sent 1:12 a.m.

Past midnight the river went over the lip of the old core's lowest canal. Water stood in the street to the height of a kerb, then a step.

Natalie and Isabel were at a corner in the north lanes. Something in the brickwork there might have needed cutting. Neither had decided. Then Natalie's patch stirred near the canal bridge, hard and low, and her line pulled her south across the city. She went. She told Isabel to wait and not to touch it.

Isabel waited eleven minutes. Then she put on the line's shape and made the cut herself. The thing in the brick was the Hundred and Ninth: Creeping Knotweed. Her hands shook before she started. Halfway through they gave out. The cut hung open in the wall, copper at its edges, not finished.

She stayed in the line's shape after that, standing in the water.

Natalie came back up the lanes at a run, wet to the knee. She stepped between Isabel and the wall and took the cut out of her hands. It bit back. A burn went across both of Natalie's palms, copper-dark, on top of the cold. The cut closed crooked.

The patch at the canal bridge had gone quiet by then. No one went to see what it had done.

Log

  • The river breaks its banks at the old core's lowest canal in the storm, and Natalie feels her patch stir hard and deep near the canal bridge; her line pulls her back across the city while Isabel stands at a north-lanes corner that might need a cut. (failure, risky, rolled 3)
    • Isabel and Natalie -1
    • Isabel now believes: Natalie went still and far away at the corner — she's already decided to leave, and it's because of something Isabel did.
    • Natalie now believes: The old core is awake and pulling her back — the canal bridge is where the trouble is.
  • Isabel gets her shaking hands into the corner cut herself, before Natalie can check it.
    • Isabel's hands give out on a cut +1
  • Natalie steps in front of Isabel and takes the cut out of her shaking hands. (failure, desperate, rolled 2, 3)
    • Natalie hurt: takes the blight cut into her own hands at the flooded corner and it bites back — a burn across her hands on top of the cold
    • Isabel now believes: Natalie took the cut out of her hands because she's decided Isabel can't be trusted with the work.

entry.title: Day 1: The Girl Who Walked a Half Step Ahead
entry.content:
Lower Bridge shelter closed for repairs until further notice. Please allow extra time.a River Tram service notice

At four in the morning the downstairs neighbour sent a message. Hoshi had been yowling at the same corner of the flat for an hour. Come and deal with your cat.

Isabel was dressed before she woke Natalie. She said the cat needed her. She named the bridge she would take and how long it would be. She said nothing else. Her keys were already in her hand.

Natalie got up and put on her coat. No one had asked her to. She said she would walk with her, and held the door.

The rain came off the river sideways. The south ridge towers blinked red through it. They crossed at the lower bridge, where there was no shelter. Natalie's coat was not made for weather. By the second street it was black with water at the shoulders and cuffs, and her shoes had filled. She put her hands in her pockets. They did not stop shaking.

Isabel walked a half step ahead the whole way.

Log

  • Isabel's downstairs neighbour messages at four in the morning to say Hoshi has been yowling at the same corner of the flat for an hour, and asks her to come and deal with her cat. (clean, risky, rolled 6)
  • Isabel wakes Natalie, says only that the cat needs her, and leaves the flat without mentioning last night or the kiss. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 4)
    • Isabel and Natalie -1
  • Natalie pulls on her coat without being asked and quietly offers to walk with Isabel through the rain to her flat. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 5)
    • Natalie hurt: soaked through and chilled to the bone, out in the sideways rain at four in the morning on no sleep
    • Isabel now believes: That Natalie came with her out of pity, and that Natalie's silence about the kiss means she has decided it was a mistake.
    • Natalie now believes: That going with her tonight is what stands between Isabel and the thing Natalie did at twenty-six.
